summary:
**Lunar & Martian Time Capsule**

Lunar & Martian Time Capsule is an interactive digital archive that explores the human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. We aim to develop a web-based platform featuring interactive maps, photographs, and detailed stories of discarded spacecraft components, scientific instruments, landing equipment, and other mission remnants.

The platform will allow users to explore where these objects are located, which missions they belong to, why they were left behind, and their historical and scientific significance. By transforming mission data into an engaging visual storytelling experience, our project addresses NASA's challenge of documenting and sharing the stories of discarded space equipment.

Our goal is to preserve the legacy of space exploration, raise awareness about humanity's presence beyond Earth, and inspire curiosity about the past, present, and future of lunar and Martian missions.
details:
Project Details – Lunar & Martian Time Capsule

Lunar & Martian Time Capsule is an interactive digital archive developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge's theme, "Abandoned but not Forgotten." The project focuses on documenting human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions.

What does it do and how does it work?

The website acts as a digital museum where users can explore spacecraft components, scientific instruments, landing equipment and other mission remnants. It organizes these objects according to their locations on the Moon and Mars. Users can browse the archive, search for specific objects, filter them by planet and view additional information about their missions, purposes and historical significance.

What are its benefits?

The project makes information about space exploration remnants easier to discover and understand. It helps users recognize that objects left behind on other celestial bodies are not merely discarded equipment, but valuable evidence of humanity's exploration beyond Earth. It also provides an accessible way to learn about past lunar and Martian missions.

What is its intended impact?

Our aim is to preserve the stories behind these objects, increase awareness of humanity's presence beyond Earth and encourage curiosity about space exploration. The project highlights the historical and scientific value of mission remnants and helps ensure that these important parts of space history are not forgotten.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a web-based prototype using:

  • HTML – to structure the website and its content.
  • CSS – to design the interface, layout and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript – to implement interactive elements such as searching, filtering and displaying object details.
  • Visual Studio Code – as the development environment.
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages – for source-code hosting and website deployment.

No additional hardware or backend database was required for the prototype.

What makes the project creative?

The project presents space exploration history through the concept of a digital time capsule. Instead of focusing only on successful missions and their achievements, it draws attention to the objects that remain after missions are completed. By organizing these remnants into an accessible digital archive, it transforms technical mission information into an engaging learning experience.

What factors were considered?

The project considered accessibility, simplicity, educational value, ease of navigation and the importance of preserving accurate mission information. The website was designed to make exploration straightforward for users while keeping the focus on the stories and significance of objects left on the Moon and Mars.
